The exact-title article is **PMID 27499270**, published in *Journal of Cardiology* in 2017.

In this cohort of 110 patients with paroxysmal AF undergoing second-generation cryoballoon ablation, 20 (18%) had recurrence over a mean 9-month follow-up. Higher eGFR was associated with lower recurrence hazard (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.93–0.99; p=0.047). Recurrence rates were 7% for eGFR ≥90, 12% for eGFR 60–89.9, and 46% for eGFR 30–59.9 mL/min/1.73 m².

Non-PV ectopic beats were also an independent recurrence predictor (HR 2.92, 95% CI 1.03–8.27) and were more common in the lower-eGFR groups. The authors proposed these foci might be related to poorer outcomes; the abstract shows an association, not proof that non-PV triggers explain or mediate the renal-function effect. **Evidence source:** PMID 27499270 abstract, retrieved via the article-content tool.

**Yes.** The 2017 study (PMID 27499270) followed 110 patients with paroxysmal AF after second-generation cryoballoon ablation; 20 (18%) had recurrence over a mean of 9 months. Recurrence rose across lower eGFR categories: 7% with eGFR ≥90, 12% with eGFR 60–89.9, and 46% with eGFR 30–59.9 mL/min/1.73 m². Higher eGFR was associated with lower recurrence hazard (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.93–0.99; p=0.047). [Source: `call_7zxwgWaMEEajIlD90iKFRMEB`]

Non-pulmonary-vein ectopic beats were also associated with recurrence (HR 2.92, 95% CI 1.03–8.27) and were more common at lower eGFR. This supports the authors’ proposed link, but does **not** establish that non-PV foci mediate the renal-function association. The evidence comes from a relatively small observational cohort with limited follow-up. [Source: `call_7zxwgWaMEEajIlD90iKFRMEB`]

FINAL DECISION: YES
